question_or_decision: Which word marks a requirement? Options: "must" (approved in STE) or "shall" (used in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, not approved in STE).
selected_answer_or_effect: Each PRD requirement uses "must". The conventions section of each PRD defines the word.

question_or_decision: Does the PRD set have a project dictionary?
selected_answer_or_effect: Yes. An appendix lists the approved technical nouns and technical verbs of the project. The product owner gave no company term list, so the PRD set starts a new list.

question_or_decision: Does the validator check the text of needs and requirements against STE?
selected_answer_or_effect: Yes, as an optional rule set: sentence length, approved modal verbs, passive voice and the project dictionary. The tool does not claim full STE compliance.

question_or_decision: Who uses the product? Is it internal, open source or commercial?
selected_answer_or_effect: Internal product. The three user roles are: systems engineer (needs and requirements), software developer (application model) and platform engineer (infrastructure).

question_or_decision: How is the toolchain delivered?
selected_answer_or_effect: A CLI and a GitHub Action in phase 1. A VS Code extension with a language server comes in a later phase.

question_or_decision: Which parts are in which phase?
selected_answer_or_effect: Phase 1: the four model layers, validation, traceability, the FastAPI generator, the OpenTofu generator and the GitHub Actions generator (from Q25). Phase 2: the React generator. Phase 3: the Next.js generator.

question_or_decision: How does the DSML extend SysML v2? Options: (a) a model library with metadata definitions; (b) a new concrete syntax that compiles to SysML v2; (c) both.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a) A model library with metadata definitions. Models are standard SysML v2 textual notation with user-defined keywords, for example `#Need` and `#Entity`. All compliant tools can read the models.

question_or_decision: Which engine parses the model? Which language does the toolchain use? Options: OMG Pilot Implementation, OpenSysML, sysml2kit, Sensmetry Syside, our own parser.
selected_answer_or_effect: OpenSysML is the SysML v2 engine. The engine stays behind a versioned intermediate model (IR). Generators and validators read only the IR. Python is the toolchain language, and uv manages the Python project.

question_or_decision: What is the source of truth for the model?
selected_answer_or_effect: Textual `.sysml` files in Git. Import from a Systems Modeling API server comes in a later phase. The PRD set does not require a graphical tool.

question_or_decision: How do elements keep a stable identity?
selected_answer_or_effect: Each need, requirement and verification has a mandatory short name, for example `<'R-001'>`. Other elements use their qualified name. The validator reports a rename as an identity change against the Git baseline. The ID format is open (decision record 02).

question_or_decision: Which attributes do needs and requirements have?
selected_answer_or_effect: Core set: ID, title, text, rationale, priority (MoSCoW), status, source and owner. Requirements also have a kind: functional, performance, security, interface or constraint. Users can add attributes through the DSML library. The set of mandatory attributes is open (decision record 02).

question_or_decision: Are requirements formal?
selected_answer_or_effect: Text is mandatory. A formal constraint is optional, for example `require constraint { p95Latency <= 300 [ms] }`. The validator evaluates a constraint when it refers to model attributes.

question_or_decision: Is there a verification layer?
selected_answer_or_effect: Yes. Phase 1 includes verification elements and `verify` links to test files. Test generation comes in a later phase.

section: E. Application model and code generation
question_or_decision: What does the application model contain? Option: also model behavior with SysML v2 actions and state machines.
selected_answer_or_effect: Phase 1 scope: entities (fields, types, constraints, relations); API operations (CRUD and custom operations with typed input and output); UI views (list, detail and form pages, and navigation, for React and Next.js only); security (roles and permissions for each operation and view). Business logic is not in the model. Developers write it by hand in extension points. Behavior generation is not in phase 1.

section: E. Application model and code generation
question_or_decision: How are generated code and hand-written code kept apart? Options: generation gap, protected regions, merge.
selected_answer_or_effect: Generation gap. The generator replaces generated files at each run. Hand-written code is in other files and calls or extends the generated code. There are no protected regions and no merge. A "create once" mode writes stubs for hand-written files only if they do not exist. The location of generated files changes because of AD2 and AD3 (decision record 02).

section: E. Application model and code generation
question_or_decision: What does "deterministic" mean?
selected_answer_or_effect: The same model, generator version and configuration give byte-identical output on all operating systems. Rules: sorted output, no timestamps, LF line ends, UTF-8, already-formatted template output and golden-file tests. No AI model is in the generation path. Lockfiles are outside the determinism boundary. CI makes them, and Git keeps them.

section: E. Application model and code generation
question_or_decision: Which stack does each target use?
selected_answer_or_effect: TypeScript targets: strict TypeScript and pnpm. React: Vite, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, TanStack Form with Zod, Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui. Next.js: App Router, route handlers for the REST API, Drizzle ORM and shadcn/ui. FastAPI: uv, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2 with Alembic, and pytest. Authentication: Amazon Cognito for all targets. The PRDs pin the exact versions.

section: E. Application model and code generation
question_or_decision: Can one model contain several applications?
selected_answer_or_effect: Yes. An application is one deployable unit with one target. A React app and a FastAPI service in one model use one API model. Import of an external OpenAPI file comes in phase 2.

section: E. Application model and code generation
question_or_decision: Which database? How are migrations made?
selected_answer_or_effect: PostgreSQL only in phase 1. The generator keeps a schema snapshot in Git. It writes each migration from the difference between the snapshot and the model. A destructive change (drop or rename) needs an explicit model annotation.

question_or_decision: Which abstraction level? Options: (a) AWS resources directly; (b) logical elements with an AWS binding; (c) both layers.
selected_answer_or_effect: (c) Two layers. The logical layer is cloud-neutral. The AWS layer realizes it. A second cloud adds one more realization layer.

question_or_decision: Which AWS services are in phase 1?
selected_answer_or_effect: React: S3, CloudFront, ACM and Route 53. Next.js: ECS Fargate behind an ALB. FastAPI: ECS Fargate behind an ALB. Data: RDS for PostgreSQL. Shared: VPC with public and private subnets, ECR, Secrets Manager, KMS, CloudWatch Logs and IAM roles with least privilege. Amazon Cognito is added because of Q17. SQS and Aurora Serverless are not in phase 1.

question_or_decision: OpenTofu or Terraform?
selected_answer_or_effect: HCL that both tools accept. OpenTofu is the primary CI target. Features of only one tool are available only through an option. The AWS provider major version is pinned. State is in an S3 backend with state locks.

question_or_decision: Raw resources or community modules?
selected_answer_or_effect: Raw `aws_*` resources in generated local modules. There is no external module dependency, and each resource has a trace tag.

question_or_decision: How does the model show environments?
selected_answer_or_effect: The model contains the environments dev, staging and prod. Each environment changes a small set of attributes: size, count and Multi-AZ. The generator writes one root module for each environment. The AWS account layout is open (decision record 02).

question_or_decision: How do the application and infrastructure connect? Is CI/CD generation in phase 1?
selected_answer_or_effect: The application generator writes the Dockerfile. The IaC generator writes ECR, the service and the task definition, with the image tag as a variable. The toolchain generates CI/CD pipelines for GitHub Actions in phase 1.

question_or_decision: Where do the rules live? Options: (a) SysML v2 constraints in the DSML library; (b) code rules that read the IR; (c) both.
selected_answer_or_effect: (b) Python code rules that read the IR in phase 1. Each rule has an ID, a severity, a message and a fix hint.

question_or_decision: Which rule categories?
selected_answer_or_effect: 1. SysML v2 well-formedness (from OpenSysML). 2. DSML structure, for example: each entity has a primary key. 3. Coverage: each need has a requirement, and each requirement has a satisfying element. 4. Cross-layer: each application has an allocation, and a React-only target has no database entity. 5. AWS policy: no public database, encryption at rest, mandatory tags and name length limits. 6. Requirement text: the optional STE rule set from Q3. No company policies were given.

question_or_decision: Which output formats and gates?
selected_answer_or_effect: Text for people, JSON, and SARIF for CI and code review tools. Code generation stops if there is an error. A `#Waiver` annotation can suppress a rule, but it must have a reason and an owner. An optional output check runs `tsc`, `ruff`, `tofu validate` and `tflint` on the generated code.

question_or_decision: Which link types?
selected_answer_or_effect: Stakeholder to need: the `stakeholder` member of the concern. Need to requirement: `frame`. Requirement to requirement: derivation and refinement. Requirement to application element: `satisfy`. Application element to infrastructure element: `allocate`. Requirement to verification: `verify`.

question_or_decision: How does the trace go into code and into the cloud?
selected_answer_or_effect: Each generated file has a header with element IDs. The generator writes a sorted `trace.json` (element, file, symbol). Developers can add trace comments in hand-written code, for example `# trace: R-001`, and the tool reads them. Each AWS resource has tags with the element ID and the Git commit of the model.

question_or_decision: Which reports?
selected_answer_or_effect: Coverage matrix, orphan report, impact analysis (from a changed element to the affected requirements and files) and suspect links after a change. A Git commit is the baseline. Output formats: static HTML, CSV and JSON. All reports are deterministic.

question_or_decision: One PRD or several?
selected_answer_or_effect: Several PRD documents and one top-level document that links them. Requirement IDs have a prefix for each PRD, for example `PRD-GEN-012`. The list of PRD documents is open (decision record 02).

question_or_decision: Does an appendix write the PRD requirements in the DSML, as a `.sysml` file?
selected_answer_or_effect: No answer. The question moves to decision record 02.

question_or_decision: The language is a DSML (domain-specific modeling language). The name "DMSL" in earlier text was a typo.
selected_answer_or_effect: All documents use "DSML". The model library package is `DSML`.

question_or_decision: The React and Next.js generators use Feature-Sliced Design (FSD). FSD puts code in layers (app, pages, widgets, features, entities, shared). Each layer contains slices, and each slice contains segments.
selected_answer_or_effect: The generators map model elements to FSD layers and slices. Decision record 02 sets the mapping, the Next.js folder layout and the location of server code.

question_or_decision: The FastAPI generator uses vertical slice architecture. Each feature is one slice that contains its route, schemas, handler and data access.
selected_answer_or_effect: The generator writes one folder for each slice. Decision record 02 sets the slice size and the shared code.

question_or_decision: Where do generated files go? Options: (a) a top-level `gen/` folder, as in the Q15 default (it breaks FSD and vertical slices); (b) in each slice, in the segment that agrees with the purpose of the file, with a name suffix; (c) in each slice, in a separate `generated` folder.
selected_answer_or_effect: (b). Generated file names end with `.gen.ts`, `.gen.tsx` or `_gen.py`. The generator writes and deletes only these files. Each slice has a public API file (`index.ts`) that the "create once" mode writes. It re-exports `index.gen.ts`, and developers can add exports to it. The Next.js `app/` folder is fully generated, because Next.js sets its file names.

question_or_decision: How do model elements map to FSD layers in React and Next.js?
selected_answer_or_effect: Entity: `entities/<entity>` (types, Zod schemas, TanStack Query hooks). Custom operation or form action: `features/<operation>` (TanStack Form form, mutation). List and detail blocks: `widgets/<entity>-list` and `widgets/<entity>-details`. View: `pages/<view>`. Router, providers, navigation and authentication start: `app`. API client, shadcn/ui components, authentication client and configuration: `shared/api`, `shared/ui`, `shared/auth` and `shared/config`.

question_or_decision: How does Next.js agree with FSD, and where is the server code? Options: (a) the layout of the FSD guide for Next.js, in one package; (b) a monorepo with an FSD web package and a server package with vertical slices.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a). The Next.js `app/` folder is at the project root and contains only route files that re-export from FSD. The FSD layers are in `src/`, and the layers app and pages have the names `_app` and `_pages`. Route handlers are in `src/_app/api-routes`. Each slice exports its server-only code (data access, business logic) through `index.server.ts`. The Drizzle schema and queries are in `src/shared/db`.

question_or_decision: What is the size of a FastAPI slice, and where is shared code? Options: one slice for each operation, or one slice for each entity.
selected_answer_or_effect: One slice for each operation, in one folder for each entity: `app/features/<entity>/<operation>/`. A slice contains `endpoint_gen.py` (router), `schemas_gen.py` (Pydantic models) and `handler.py` (hand-written, create once). SQLAlchemy table models are shared in `app/shared/db/models/`. The database session, the Cognito token check, the configuration and the error types are in `app/shared/`. `app/main_gen.py` registers all slice routers in sorted order. Alembic migrations are in `migrations/`.

question_or_decision: How does Python call OpenSysML? Options: (a) the `opensysml` Python client; (b) the `sysml` CLI as a subprocess; (c) a Go adapter program that writes the IR.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a). The [opensysml](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/Open-MBEE/OpenSysML) Python client uses gRPC and starts `sysml-grpc` as a private child process. One release tag gives the Python package and the binary, so the toolchain pins one version for both (0.9.2, released on 5 October 2026). OpenSysML is not yet at version 1.0. An IR adapter isolates its API, and golden IR tests run at each version change.

question_or_decision: Which route mode does TanStack Router use? Options: (a) file-based routing, which TanStack recommends: a build plugin writes the route tree from a `routes/` folder; (b) code-based routing; (c) virtual file routes.
selected_answer_or_effect: (b). The DSML generator writes the route tree in `src/app/router/routes.gen.tsx`, and each route imports a page slice. A `routes/` folder is not an FSD layer, and a build plugin adds a second code generator. The model already gives the route tree.

question_or_decision: Does Next.js also use TanStack Form?
selected_answer_or_effect: Yes, for client-side forms. The server uses the same Zod schemas to validate the input again.

question_or_decision: Where does the shadcn/ui source come from? The shadcn/ui CLI copies component source from a registry when it runs, and the registry can change. Options: (a) the CLI at generation time; (b) a pinned copy in the generator package.
selected_answer_or_effect: (b). The generator package holds a pinned copy of the shadcn/ui components that its templates use. The generator writes them to `shared/ui` in "create once" mode, so developers own them and can change them. A generator release updates the copy.

question_or_decision: How does each target use Cognito? Options for the web clients: (a) the AWS Amplify Auth library; (b) a general OIDC library (`oidc-client-ts` for React, Auth.js for Next.js).
selected_answer_or_effect: Infrastructure: one user pool for each environment, one app client for each application, and one user pool group for each model role. Login uses Cognito managed login with the authorization code flow and PKCE. React and Next.js: (a) Amplify Auth, so both targets use one library. In Next.js, the Amplify adapter for Next.js keeps the tokens in cookies, so server code can read the session. FastAPI: a shared dependency in `app/shared/auth` checks the JWT access token against the JWKS of the user pool and maps the `cognito:groups` claim to model roles. The web clients send the access token as a bearer token. The PRDs check the current library versions.

question_or_decision: Which pipelines does the toolchain generate for GitHub Actions?
selected_answer_or_effect: AWS access: GitHub OIDC and one IAM role for each environment, with no long-term access keys. Pull request: model validation with SARIF upload to code scanning; a determinism check (run the generator again, then `git diff --exit-code` must find no change); build, lint and tests of each application; `tofu plan` for dev, with the plan in the job summary. Main branch: build the images, push them to ECR, then `tofu apply` and deploy to dev. Promotion: a release tag or a manual run moves the same image digest to staging and then to prod. A GitHub environment with required reviewers protects prod. Generated code is in Git. Actions are pinned to commit SHAs. Workflow files are in `.github/workflows/` and their names end with `.gen.yml`.

question_or_decision: Which AWS account layout? Options: (a) one account for all environments; (b) one account for each environment; (c) one account for each environment, plus a shared tooling account for ECR.
selected_answer_or_effect: (c). The tooling account holds ECR, and each environment account pulls images by digest. Each environment account holds its own OpenTofu state bucket and its own deploy role. AWS Organizations manages the accounts.

question_or_decision: Which ID format do needs, requirements and verifications use? Option: also add an OpenSysML `IdentityMetadata::ElementId` annotation, so a rename keeps the identity.
selected_answer_or_effect: `N-001` for needs, `R-001` for requirements and `V-001` for verifications. The number has a minimum of three digits with leading zeros. Each ID is unique in the model, and a deleted ID is not used again. The ID is the SysML v2 short name, for example `<'R-001'>`, and the toolchain uses it as the trace ID. ElementId annotations are not mandatory. A project can set a different ID pattern in its configuration.

question_or_decision: Which attributes are mandatory?
selected_answer_or_effect: Need: ID, title, text, stakeholder, priority and status. Requirement: ID, title, text, kind, priority and status. Verification: ID, title and method (test, analysis, inspection or demonstration). Rationale, source and owner are optional. Status values: draft, approved, implemented, verified and retired.

question_or_decision: Which documents are in the PRD set? Option: fewer documents, for example CI/CD in the IaC PRD and the core in the DSML PRD.
selected_answer_or_effect: The eight documents in the table below. The application generation PRD has one tab for the common rules and one tab for each target.

question_or_decision: Does an appendix write the PRD requirements in the DSML? (Q33 had no answer.)
selected_answer_or_effect: Yes. The top-level PRD has a second tab that holds all PRD requirements and product needs as one `.sysml` text in the DSML. The short name of each requirement is its PRD ID, for example `<'PRD-DSML-001'>`. OpenSysML must parse the text with no errors. This is the first test of the DSML.

question_or_decision: Which versions does the toolchain pin? Options: (a) exact patch versions in the PRDs now; (b) release lines in this record, and exact patch versions in one version file in the toolchain repository; (c) the newest version at each generation. Option (c) breaks determinism.
selected_answer_or_effect: (b). Pin the phase 1 lines in the table below. The first phase 1 release fixes the exact patch versions in the version file, and later toolchain releases update it. A new decision record sets the TypeScript lines at the start of phase 2.

question_or_decision: Which operating systems does the toolchain support, and how fast must it be?
selected_answer_or_effect: Operating systems: Linux x64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64. Windows only through WSL. Performance: `dsml validate` and `dsml generate` on a model with 1,000 elements must finish in less than 10 seconds on a GitHub-hosted Linux runner with 4 vCPUs. The toolchain must accept models with up to 10,000 elements.

question_or_decision: Does the FastAPI target use synchronous or asynchronous database access? Options: (a) asynchronous SQLAlchemy with the psycopg 3 driver; (b) synchronous SQLAlchemy with psycopg 3; (c) asynchronous with asyncpg.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a). FastAPI endpoints are `async def`, and the session is an `AsyncSession`. psycopg 3 supports the two modes, so a change to (b) later needs no new driver.

question_or_decision: Who writes the handler of a CRUD operation? Options: (a) the generator writes a full handler (`handler_gen.py`), and only custom operations get a hand-written stub; (b) each operation gets a create-once stub.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a). CRUD handlers are standard code, so a stub would make each developer write the same code. To change a CRUD operation, a developer models it as a custom operation.

question_or_decision: Who owns the dependency lists (`pyproject.toml`, `package.json`)? Options: (a) the generator owns them, and extra dependencies come from `dsml.toml`; (b) they are create-once files that developers own, and `dsml check-output` warns if a pinned version is different from the baseline.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a). The generator writes the pinned dependencies of the baseline and the extra dependencies of the configuration file, and the generated CI fails if the lockfile does not agree. This keeps PRD-TOP-008 true for each commit.

question_or_decision: How does the Git commit of the model reach AWS? Options: (a) the tag `dsml:model-commit` on each resource, from a plan-time variable, as Q30 selected; (b) only the tag `dsml:element` on each resource, and the commit in one SSM parameter for each environment and in the deploy summary; (c) the commit tag only on resources whose element changed.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a), because Q30 selected it. Effect: each deployment of a new commit updates the tags of all taggable resources in place, with no downtime, and each plan shows these tag updates. Option (b) gives plans that show only real changes. Option (c) needs state that the toolchain does not have.

question_or_decision: When do database migrations run? Options: (a) a one-off ECS task with the new image, before the services move to the new task definition; (b) at container start; (c) by hand.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a). A failed migration stops the deployment before any service changes. With (b), each task of a service tries to migrate at the same time.

question_or_decision: Which baseline do `impact` and `suspect` use when the user gives no `--baseline`? Options: (a) the newest release tag `v*` before `HEAD`; (b) the merge base with the main branch; (c) a Git tag `trace-baseline` that a systems engineer moves after each review.
selected_answer_or_effect: (a). A release is the point where the team accepts the trace state. A team that reviews more often can set (c) in the configuration file.
